headline: Rayo dominate but keep drawing — and Vallecas is partly closed
summary: Rayo Vallecano made chances worth 2.26 goals at Getafe on Sunday and drew 1-1 — the flat derby we expected. On Saturday they host Elche at Vallecas, a ground that will be partly closed after the crowd trouble at their last home game. Elche managed 0.3 expected goals at Villarreal, sit 18th on 7 points and have one win in nine league games. Rayo keep defender Pathé Ciss, available after his fifth yellow card was overturned. Across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, Rayo are 54% favourites, rated about two-thirds of a goal better, with over 2.5 goals at 52.4%. A narrow home win is the shape of it.
read: Rayo Vallecano are 54% favourites at home against an Elche side sitting 18th with one win in nine league games. Rayo out-created Getafe 2.26 to 0.61 on Sunday yet drew 1-1, while Elche average just 0.86 xG per game and travel to a Vallecas that will be partially closed.

facts.fact: Rayo Vallecano are clear home favourites at 54.0% to win.
facts.meaning: The market makes Rayo more likely than not to take all three points at Vallecas.

facts.fact: Vallecas will be partially closed for this match, with only 143 tickets made available to Elche fans.
Rayo out-created Getafe 2.26 xG to 0.61 on Sunday.
facts.meaning: They are generating a high volume of quality chances, so the goals should keep coming even if results have been draws.

facts.fact: Elche managed just 0.3 xG in their 0-0 at Villarreal.
facts.meaning: Away from home they create almost nothing, so a point is the realistic target at Vallecas.

facts.fact: Elche go into the game 18th in La Liga, in the relegation zone.
facts.meaning: They arrive at Vallecas needing a result rather than choosing how to chase one.

facts.fact: Elche will be without midfielder Marc Aguado, their only absentee, who has played 375 minutes this season.
facts.meaning: Elche are otherwise at full strength, so their defensive shape should be close to what the coach wants.

facts.fact: Rayo defender Pathé Ciss, who has played 765 minutes this season, is available after his fifth yellow card was overturned on appeal.
facts.meaning: Rayo keep a regular starter for a game in which they will have most of the ball and need to guard against counters.

facts.fact: The market rates Rayo about two-thirds of a goal better than Elche, with a fair handicap line of -0.67.
facts.meaning: A narrow Rayo win is the expected shape of the game, not a rout.

sources.fact: Rayo Vallecano will serve a partial stadium closure and a €6,000 fine for the match against Elche, with only 143 tickets available to Elche fans.
Rayo Vallecano supporters' groups reject the punishment and maintain their protests against club president Martín Presa.
Pathé Ciss will be available to play against Elche after the Disciplinary Committee overturned his fifth yellow card of the season following a successful Rayo appeal.
Rayo Vallecano players did not train at the Ciudad Deportiva 72 hours before the Elche match, according to Mundo Deportivo.
Rayo Vallecano drew 1-1 at Getafe in their previous La Liga match, having taken the lead and playing over an hour with a numerical advantage for Getafe.

Spain's anti-violence commission has proposed bans and fines for 12 Rayo Vallecano supporters who threw paper airplanes and other objects onto the pitch, forcing the suspension of the La Liga match against Athletic Bilbao.
Elche goalkeeper Matías Dituro said the team is "on the right track" and "growing", noting they have taken five points from the last three games but "need to get a win" against Rayo Vallecano.
Dituro credited Elche's growth to the work of coach Anselmi and urged focus on the match at Vallecas.
